lem-scaled-chebyshev-filter-bound-on-a-s:
## Statement

Let $a>b>c$ be real numbers, let $k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\ge0$, and put

$$\xi(x):=\frac{2x-b-c}{b-c},\qquad \xi_a:=\xi(a)=1+\frac{2(a-b)}{b-c}>1.$$

Define

$$p_k(x):=\frac{T_k(\xi(x))}{T_k(\xi_a)},$$

where $T_k$ is the $k$th Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind from
[[def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind]]. Then $p_k(a)=1$ and

$$\max_{x\in[c,b]}|p_k(x)|=\frac{1}{T_k(\xi_a)}.$$
thm-two-pass-mgs-arnoldi-local-relation-:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, and let the computed starting
vector $q_1$ be nonzero. Fix $m\ge1$ and, for $j=1,\ldots,m$, compute each component of
$z_j=\operatorname{fl}(Aq_j)$ by the length-$n$ rounded dot product of that
row with $q_j$. Then perform two complete modified Gram–Schmidt passes: for
$p=1,2$ and $i=1,\ldots,j$, compute
$$h_{ij}^{(p)}=\operatorname{fl}(q_i^{\mathsf T}w_{i-1,j}^{(p)}),\qquad w_{ij}^{(p)}=\operatorname{fl}(w_{i-1,j}^{(p)}-h_{ij}^{(p)}q_i),$$
where $w_{0j}^{(1)}=z_j$ and $w_{0j}^{(2)}=w_{jj}^{(1)}$. The vector update
is componentwise one rounded product followed by one rounded subtraction.
Store $h_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}(h_{ij}^{(1)}+h_{ij}^{(2)})$. Compute
$t_j=\operatorname{fl}((w_{jj}^{(2)})^{\mathsf T}w_{jj}^{(2)})$ as a
length-$n$ dot product, $\beta_{j+1}=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{t_j})$, and
$q_{j+1}=\operatorname{fl}(w_{jj}^{(2)}/\beta_{j+1})$ componentwise.

Assume all products, partial sums, square roots, divisions, and updates used
here succeed in the operationwise model, $nu<1$, $\gamma_n<1$, $2u<1$, and
$t_j>0$. Define $c_n=(1-u)\sqrt{1-\gamma_n}$. Then
$\beta_{j+1}\ge c_n\|w_{jj}^{(2)}\|_2>0$, and the computed columns satisfy
$$Aq_j=\sum_{i=1}^j h_{ij}q_i+\beta_{j+1}q_{j+1}+e_j,$$
where, writing $\delta_j^{mv}=z_j-Aq_j$,
$$e_j=-\delta_j^{norm}-\delta_j^{mv} -\sum_{p=1}^2\sum_{i=1}^j\zeta_{ij}^{(p)} -\sum_{i=1}^j\chi_{ij}q_i,$$
with $\delta_j^{norm}=\beta_{j+1}q_{j+1}-w_{jj}^{(2)}$,
$\zeta_{ij}^{(p)}=w_{ij}^{(p)}-(w_{i-1,j}^{(p)}-h_{ij}^{(p)}q_i)$, and
$\chi_{ij}=h_{ij}-(h_{ij}^{(1)}+h_{ij}^{(2)})$. These errors obey
$$\|\delta_j^{mv}\|_2\le\gamma_n \left(\sum_{a=1}^n\left(\sum_{b=1}^n|A_{ab}|\,|q_{j,b}|\right)^2\right)^{1/2}, \quad \|\delta_j^{norm}\|_2\le u\|w_{jj}^{(2)}\|_2,$$
$$|h_{ij}^{(p)}-q_i^{\mathsf T}w_{i-1,j}^{(p)}| \le\gamma_n\|q_i\|_1\|w_{i-1,j}^{(p)}\|_1,$$
$$\|\zeta_{ij}^{(p)}\|_2\le\gamma_2\bigl( \|w_{i-1,j}^{(p)}\|_2+|h_{ij}^{(p)}|\|q_i\|_2\bigr),\qquad |\chi_{ij}|\le u|h_{ij}^{(1)}+h_{ij}^{(2)}|.$$

If the generated vectors $q_1,\ldots,q_{m+1}$ have full column rank, there
is also an explicit conditioning-dependent orthogonality recurrence.
Put $\nu_\ell=|\|q_\ell\|_2^2-1|$ and $c_{\ell i}=q_\ell^{\mathsf T}q_i$.
For fixed $j$ and $\ell\le j$, set
$$G_{\ell j}^{0}=|q_\ell^{\mathsf T}z_j|.$$
For each pass $p$, with $h_i=h_{ij}^{(p)}$ and
$\zeta_i=\zeta_{ij}^{(p)}$, define
$$\begin{aligned} G_{\ell j}^{p}:={}&\nu_\ell\left(G_{\ell j}^{p-1}+ \sum_{i<\ell}(|h_i||c_{\ell i}|+\|q_\ell\|_2\|\zeta_i\|_2)\right) +(1+\nu_\ell)\gamma_n\|q_\ell\|_1\|w_{\ell-1,j}^{(p)}\|_1\\ &+\|q_\ell\|_2\|\zeta_\ell\|_2 +\sum_{i>\ell}(|h_i||c_{\ell i}|+\|q_\ell\|_2\|\zeta_i\|_2). \end{aligned}$$
Then the off-diagonal inner products satisfy
$$|q_\ell^{\mathsf T}q_{j+1}| \le\frac{G_{\ell j}^{2}}{\beta_{j+1}} +\frac{u\|q_\ell\|_2}{c_n}.$$
Consequently the Frobenius norm of the Gram defect of $Q_{m+1}$ is at most
$$\left(\sum_{i=1}^{m+1}\nu_i^2+ 2\sum_{1\le\ell<i\le m+1} \left(\frac{G_{\ell,i-1}^{2}}{\beta_i} +\frac{u\|q_\ell\|_2}{c_n}\right)^2\right)^{1/2},$$
where $\|B\|_F=(\sum_{a,b}|B_{ab}|^2)^{1/2}$. A zero $t_j$ is a
breakdown branch with no division or new vector; failure of any stated
rounding or positivity hypothesis makes the bound inconclusive.
thm-cg-recursive-residual-gap-and-attain:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite, let
$Ax_*=b$, and suppose the computed CG process from
[[def-conjugate-gradient-recurrence]] completes steps $k=0,\ldots,j-1$ in
the no-range-failure model of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].
Assume $nu<1$ and $2u<1$, and that every product and partial sum in each
length-$n$ matrix-vector dot product is normal-range. Write the actual stored
scalars and vectors as $\alpha_k,\hat x_k,\hat r_k,\hat p_k$, and compute
each component of $\hat q_k=\operatorname{fl}(A\hat p_k)$ by a rounded
length-$n$ dot product. Compute the updates componentwise as
$$\hat x_{k+1}=\operatorname{fl}(\hat x_k+ \operatorname{fl}(\alpha_k\hat p_k)),\qquad \hat r_{k+1}=\operatorname{fl}(\hat r_k- \operatorname{fl}(\alpha_k\hat q_k)),$$
where the inner products and outer additions/subtractions are rounded
operations and $\alpha_k$ is the actual stored scalar used by the algorithm.
Define the resulting update errors by
$$\delta^x_k:=\hat x_{k+1}-(\hat x_k+\alpha_k\hat p_k),\qquad \delta^r_k:=\hat r_{k+1}-(\hat r_k-\alpha_k\hat q_k).$$
For any index $j$ reached by the process, define
$$g_j:=\hat r_j-(b-A\hat x_j),\qquad \Gamma_j:=\|g_0\|_2+\sum_{k<j} \bigl(\|\delta^r_k\|_2+\|A\|_2\|\delta^x_k\|_2+ |\alpha_k|\|\delta^A_k\|_2\bigr).$$
Here $\|A\|_2$ is the induced Euclidean operator norm. Then
$$\|g_j\|_2\le\Gamma_j, \qquad \|b-A\hat x_j\|_2\le\|\hat r_j\|_2+\Gamma_j.$$
If $\lambda_{\min}>0$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $A$, then
$$\|x_*-\hat x_j\|_A\le \frac{\|b-A\hat x_j\|_2}{\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}}} \le\frac{\|\hat r_j\|_2+\Gamma_j}{\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}}},$$
where $\|e\|_A=\sqrt{e^{\mathsf T}Ae}$. The explicit operation errors obey
$$\|\delta^A_k\|_2\le\gamma_n \left(\sum_{i=1}^n\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^n |A_{i\ell}|\,|\hat p_{k,\ell}|\right)^2\right)^{1/2},$$
and, when $2u<1$,
$$\|\delta^x_k\|_2\le\gamma_2 \bigl(\|\hat x_k\|_2+|\alpha_k|\|\hat p_k\|_2\bigr),\quad \|\delta^r_k\|_2\le\gamma_2 \bigl(\|\hat r_k\|_2+|\alpha_k|\|\hat q_k\|_2\bigr).$$
No exact-grade termination or monotonicity of the true residual is asserted.
thm-lanczos-largest-ritz-value-chebyshev:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric with ordered eigenvalues
$\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n$. Let $r$ be the multiplicity of $\lambda_1$.
If $r<n$, assume $\lambda_1>\lambda_{r+1}$, and let $P$ be the orthogonal
projection onto the $\lambda_1$-eigenspace. Let $b\in\mathbb R^n$ be a unit
vector and, for $m\ge1$, define

$$K_m:=\operatorname{span}\{b,Ab,\ldots,A^{m-1}b\},\qquad \theta_m:=\max_{0\ne x\in K_m}\frac{x^{\mathsf T}Ax}{x^{\mathsf T}x}.$$

Thus $\theta_m$ is the largest Rayleigh–Ritz value on $K_m$; if Lanczos runs
through step $m$ without breakdown, it is the largest Ritz value of
$Q_m^{\mathsf T}AQ_m$. If $r=n$, then $A=\lambda_1I$ and $\theta_m=\lambda_1$
for every $m\ge1$. Suppose $r<n$.

1. If $Pb=0$, then $\theta_m\le\lambda_{r+1}$ for every $m$; no convergence
   to $\lambda_1$ is asserted.

2. If $Pb\ne0$, put
   $$\tau:=\frac{\|(I-P)b\|_2}{\|Pb\|_2}.$$
   If $\lambda_{r+1}>\lambda_n$, then for every $m\ge1$,
   $$0\le\lambda_1-\theta_m\le \frac{(\lambda_1-\lambda_n)\tau^2} {T_{m-1}\!\left(1+2\frac{\lambda_1-\lambda_{r+1}} {\lambda_{r+1}-\lambda_n}\right)^2}.$$
   For a simple top eigenvalue ($r=1$), $\tau$ is the tangent of the angle
   between $b$ and a unit top eigenvector, so the starting-angle denominator
   is explicit.

3. If $\lambda_{r+1}=\lambda_n$, then
   $$\lambda_1-\theta_1=(\lambda_1-\lambda_n) \frac{\|(I-P)b\|_2^2}{\|b\|_2^2},\qquad \theta_m=\lambda_1\quad(m\ge2).$$

When $r<n$, $Pb\ne0$, and exact Lanczos breakdown occurs at dimension $d$, then
$\theta_d=\lambda_1$ and $K_m=K_d$ for all $m\ge d$. These are exact-arithmetic
claims; they give no finite-precision grade-termination guarantee.
thm-gmres-true-residual-gap-from-compute:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ with $n\ge1$, let $r_0=b-Ax_0$, and let
$m\ge1$. Put $Q_m=[q_1\ \cdots\ q_m]$,
$Q_{m+1}=[q_1\ \cdots\ q_{m+1}]$, and
$\bar H_m\in\mathbb R^{(m+1)\times m}$. Suppose computed Arnoldi vectors
satisfy
$$AQ_m=Q_{m+1}\bar H_m+E_m,$$
where the columns of $E_m$ are the local error vectors of
[[thm-two-pass-mgs-arnoldi-local-relation-and-orthogonality-bound]]. Let
$I$ be the $(m+1)$-by-$(m+1)$ identity and
$\bar G=Q_{m+1}^{\mathsf T}Q_{m+1}-I$ and
$\eta=\|\bar G\|_F$, where $\|B\|_F=(\sum_{a,b}|B_{ab}|^2)^{1/2}$.
Suppose
$$r_0=\beta_1q_1+\delta_0,\qquad \hat x=x_0+Q_my+\delta_x,$$
where $y\in\mathbb R^m$ is the coefficient vector returned by the computed
GMRES least-squares stage and $\delta_x$ is the update error (zero for an
exact vector update). Define $e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{m+1}$
and the Arnoldi-coordinate least-squares residual
$$g:=\beta_1e_1-\bar H_my,$$
using the stored computed values, and let $r=b-A\hat x$ be the exact true
residual. Then
$$\|r-Q_{m+1}g\|_2\le \|\delta_0\|_2+\|E_m\|_2\|y\|_2+\|A\|_2\|\delta_x\|_2,$$
and
$$\|r\|_2\le\sqrt{1+\eta}\,\|g\|_2+ \|\delta_0\|_2+\|E_m\|_2\|y\|_2+\|A\|_2\|\delta_x\|_2.$$
Matrix $2$-norms are induced by Euclidean vector norms. If the true residual is
recomputed by rounded row dot products and rounded subtraction, with no-range
failure, write $\widehat{Ax}$ for the computed product and
$\hat r=\operatorname{fl}(b-\widehat{Ax})$. Then
$$\bigl|\|\hat r\|_2-\|r\|_2\bigr|\le\rho_{rec},\qquad \rho_{rec}:=\left(\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^2\right)^{1/2},$$
where
$$d_i:=\gamma_n\sum_{j=1}^n|A_{ij}|\,|\hat x_j| +u|b_i-\widehat{Ax}_i|.$$
No accuracy claim is made for the least-squares solve: its computed $y$ and
the resulting $g$ appear explicitly.
prop-sparse-unrestarted-gmres-work-and-s:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ have a canonical CSR representation, with
$n\ge1$, at least one stored entry in every row, and
$s=\operatorname{nnz}(A)$. Let $r_0=b-Ax_0\ne0$ and $1\le m\le n$. Run
unrestarted GMRES in exact arithmetic for at most $m$ Arnoldi columns. At
column $j$, compute one CSR matrix-vector product, orthogonalize against the
$j$ existing vectors by either one or two complete modified Gram–Schmidt
passes, and update the projected least-squares problem by applying prior
Givens rotations and forming one new rotation. Each Givens rotation is an
orthogonal $2\times2$ matrix on adjacent rows chosen to zero the current
subdiagonal entry. If Arnoldi completes $m$
columns without breakdown, solve the resulting upper-triangular least-squares
factor; if it breaks down earlier, stop at that column and make no claim about
a separate rank-deficient fallback solve. Count field arithmetic and index
work, and exclude the stored input matrix. The total work in the no-breakdown
branch is $O(ms+m^2n)$ and the Krylov working storage is $O(mn)$. The same
bounds cover all matvec, orthogonalization, and projected-rotation work
actually performed before an earlier breakdown. These are operation and
storage bounds, not convergence or runtime claims.
ex-unrestarted-and-restarted-gmres-on-a-:
## Statement

Let $A=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)$, $b=(1,1)^{\mathsf T}$, and $x_0=0$.
Verify that unrestarted GMRES reaches the exact solution by step $2$, whereas
the first GMRES$(1)$ cycle leaves residual $(2/5,-1/5)^{\mathsf T}\ne0$.
ex-cg-denominator-failure-and-minres-on-:
## Statement

For $A_- =\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $b=(1,1)^{\mathsf T}$, and $x_0=0$,
compute the first CG denominator, the first MINRES least-squares problem, and
the exact solution's membership in $K_2(A_-,b)$. Contrast this with the first
CG denominator for $A_+=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)$ and the same $b,x_0$.
ex-lanczos-poorly-aligned-start-vector-d:
## Statement

Let $A=\operatorname{diag}(10,2,1)$ and
$$b=(1/100,\alpha,\alpha)^{\mathsf T},\qquad \alpha=\sqrt{9999/20000}.$$
Verify that $\|b\|_2=1$, bound the largest two-step Ritz value by
$\theta_2<9/4$, and compare the resulting gap with the Chebyshev bound from
[[thm-lanczos-largest-ritz-value-chebyshev-bound-with-degenerate-cases]].
The comparison must show that deleting the start-angle factor would make this
particular bound false.
ex-lanczos-repeated-top-zero-component-a:
## Statement

Check four branches of
[[thm-lanczos-largest-ritz-value-chebyshev-bound-with-degenerate-cases]]:
(i) $A=5I_1$; (ii) $A=\operatorname{diag}(5,5,1)$ with
$b=(1,0,1)^{\mathsf T}/\sqrt2$; (iii)
$A=\operatorname{diag}(5,2,1)$ with $b=e_2$; and (iv) the same $A$ with
$b=(e_1+e_2)/\sqrt2$. Verify the Rayleigh–Ritz values, top-eigenspace
components, and exact invariant-subspace breakdown dimensions.
